name: Democratic centralism
summary: Democratic centralism is the Leninist organizing principle that combines open debate before a decision with binding, uniform execution after it. Organs are elected from below and subordinate to higher bodies; the minority yields to the majority and the individual to the organization. Communist parties and states have applied it, with critics arguing that centralism overwhelmed democracy in practice.
scope: The Leninist party principle as set out by Lenin (1906), the Comintern conditions (1920) and the CPC constitution, and as applied in the CPSU and ruling Communist states. It is an organizational doctrine, not a full political-economic programme, so most statements are inferred from the Marxist-Leninist parties that use it. Excludes non-Leninist organizations that borrow the label.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties (Soviet, Chinese) built state-provided health systems as a socialist duty.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: a wage floor is a modest pro-worker measure, though Leninists aim at abolishing wage labor rather than reforming it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist parties using this organizing form reject market allocation in favor of planning.

public-ownership.rationale: Parties organized on this principle, as in the Comintern program, aim at socialized ownership of the commanding heights.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: taxing property-owning classes fits the Leninist program of curbing the bourgeoisie.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: Communist parties treat unions as mass organizations or 'transmission belts' under party guidance, so support is real but conditional.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists treat private property in the means of production as something to abolish, not protect.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: regulation is acceptable but falls short of the socialization the parties seek.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states expanded social provision; cutting it conflicts with their program.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: aims at social ownership, usually state-led, rather than enterprise-level worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties accepted illegal work and also security-state vigilance over internal enemies when in power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist parties generally kept drug bans; the principle itself is silent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states restricted speech that threatened order and routinely banned racist propaganda.

strong-leader.rationale: The principle stresses collective leadership; Deng Xiaoping and others criticized one-man direction as a distortion of it.

state-harmful.rationale: Democratic centralism is meant to be applied to the state as well as the party (Lenin, 1913), so the state is a tool to be used, not abolished.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties restricted private arms while the party commanded the armed forces.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: Communist states backed strong security organs, with the military under party control.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: Communist parties in power generally treated prostitution as an exploitative survival of the old order.

decide-locally.rationale: Centralism is half the name: higher-level decisions bind lower organs, and the whole party is subordinate to the Central Committee.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist penal doctrine emphasizes re-education, though used alongside harsh punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists criticize the bourgeois family, though ruling parties often turned conservative on family policy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: historically hostile in Leninist states, more varied among modern adherents, so genuinely split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet Union legalized abortion early and Communist parties mostly supported it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist parties require atheism-oriented separation and curb religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties supported anti-racism and anti-colonial equality as part of class politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Marxist tradition explains gender roles by social and economic relations.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: Leninists favor national culture 'socialist in content' yet suspect nationalism; adherents are split.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties aim at revolutionary transformation, not respect for inherited institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: internationalist outlook makes restriction of immigration unattractive, though states applied controls.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern demanded centralism within the Communist movement, but a UN-style body of mixed states is not a Leninist goal.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred: Leninist theory views free trade as serving capitalist powers; ruling parties used state-controlled foreign trade.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred: proletarian internationalism pulls one way and defense of the socialist state the other.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: Leninists distrust Western intervention as imperialism.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: internationalism favors it as an eventual goal, but ruling parties kept strict borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist states pursued rapid growth and industrialization.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: central direction suits large-scale state action, and modern Communist parties endorse climate programs.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists prize scientific-technical progress as a base for socialism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: Soviet and Chinese state planning embraced nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Comintern conditions required communists to prepare for revolutionary seizure of power, including illegal organization.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred: cadre systems value trained officials, but the party claims to represent the masses.

central-planning.rationale: Parties built on this principle took central planning as the socialist economic model; centralism was the political counterpart.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: adherents split between orthodox planning and market socialism, as in China.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: a Georgist single tax is a reformist alternative to socialization.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: curbing inherited wealth fits the socialist program.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; Leninists favor work-based entitlement but also social provision.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: socialist states shielded their industry through state control of foreign trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment is the core of the state planning that Leninist parties exercised.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: Leninists prefer collective or state ownership to dispersed small proprietors.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: abolition is the long-term communist aim, though not a near-term policy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states nationalized banking and centralized credit.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: Leninists oppose class collaboration, though party-led unions resemble state bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Communist parties using this principle claim leadership of the state, as the CPC constitution requires state organs and army to accept party leadership; the principle itself governs the party only.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents claim to be democratic in a substantive sense while rejecting multiparty liberal democracy, so they are split on the statement as worded.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: democracy within the party is by delegates and elected organs, not direct plebiscites.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: soviets were central to the early Bolshevik state, though the party came to control them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred: Lenin affirmed self-determination in principle while the party centralized in practice; adherents split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred: Marxists reject natural hierarchy, though they accept vanguard leadership.

political-violence-never.rationale: Leninist doctrine and the Comintern conditions envisage armed struggle and civil war.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists do not hold this view.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties require strict separation and state secularism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: Leninists want these as state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states pursued strong defense under party command.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: internationalism rejects ethnic nationhood as a basis of the state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Parties using the principle are Marxist-Leninist and take class struggle as the engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: socialism aims at equality but the first stage pays by work.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; collective land ownership by the state conflicts with this.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: Leninists condemn colonialism as imperialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: Communist internationalism is class-based, not civilizational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred: socialist ethics place the collective over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The principle subordinates the individual to the organization and the minority to the majority.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: split; Soviet policy was natalist and Chinese policy restrictive.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists regard industrialization as the basis of socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred: pro-technology but institution-minded, so split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; planners have been interested in computation but party leadership is primary.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred: security-minded Communist states restrict encryption, although clandestine parties used secrecy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists are progressive and see history moving toward socialism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties insist on the correct ideology, though Deng's pragmatism splits adherents.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern conditions combined legal and illegal work including parliament, while stressing party leadership.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred: Leninists defend disciplined centralist means for a freer end.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: abolition is a distant Marxist aim but not a policy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists accept the formula for the higher stage of communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred: socialist planning is defined against production for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist parties using this form hold the theory of surplus value.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Comintern's conditions and Zinoviev's theses build the party for the proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: Soviet and early Chinese practice, though later reformed in China.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: Leninist theory of imperialism holds this.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states restricted conduct for socialist order, beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The principle subordinates the individual to the collective organization.

conscription.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states used conscription and the CPC constitution places the army under party leadership.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: opposite of the Leninist concern with collective political power.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred: socialists tie freedom to material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred: Leninists locate power in classes and the party, not in media or universities.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: Leninists reject corporatist representation in favor of party and class organs.

total-state.rationale: Inferred: Communist states directed economy and culture, but the withering-away theory complicates it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred: a fascist theme foreign to Marxist-Leninist progress narratives.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred: officially anti-imperialist, though Soviet practice differed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred: rejects feudal personal loyalty; authority rests on party organs.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists see ideology as class-bound but claim their science is objective; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists treat morality as class-determined.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred: claims to serve the proletariat's interest as the general interest, but sees class conflict.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred: Leninists historically opposed Zionism, although the USSR backed Israel in 1948.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: Leninists favor worker participation but under party guidance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred: state planning does not follow balanced-budget rules.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists reject the liberal link of political and economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties rely on discipline and enforcement organs, not example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred: Lenin endorsed national self-determination as a principle.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: internationalism pulls against restriction, state practice differed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred: 'he who does not work shall not eat' is a socialist principle.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Comintern conditions demand break with reformists and class collaboration.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: opposed to Futurist destruction of heritage; Soviet museums were preserved.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: anti-imperialist front is an old Comintern theme but this is not core.

workers-nation.rationale: The Comintern required centralization on an international scale and internationalist class organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred: formal equality of the sexes is Marxist-Leninist doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds all peoples equal, so legal racial separation is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist theory of the state; the party seeks to turn it into an instrument of the working class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: no stated view; Communist states have both expanded fossil fuels and green energy.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: a conspiracy theory outside Marxist-Leninist analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: representation is through elected hierarchy, with no stated view on party-list PR.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred: Leninist internationalism has its own mission of world revolution, not national.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: Marxists acknowledge women's oppression tied to class society.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred: party criticizes bourgeois elites but not its own cadres; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: eugenic coercion contradicts the materialist, egalitarian doctrine of the parties that use this principle.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: party control of security organs means accountability runs through the party.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: a minimal state conflicts with the planning and party-led state these parties build.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist egalitarianism rejects racial hierarchy and any discouragement of mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred: formal equality accepted but the class-based treatment of enemies complicates it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern held the world party view yet Stalinist parties built socialism in one country; split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: secular equality before the law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: Communist states restrict proselytism but a dedicated conversion ban is not doctrine.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: a religious-cultural ban has no basis in Marxist-Leninist materialism or policy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin's doctrine adopted by ruling parties; centralism strengthened the state under hostile encirclement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: claims legitimacy from representing the working class, not from consent as liberals mean it.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred: rejected in principle although Soviet deportations occurred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: Communist states ban parties opposing the socialist order; the 1921 faction ban shows this logic internally.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet and Chinese systems concentrate power in people's congresses led by the party, as Liu Shaoqi said of China's 'centralized' state power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Democratic centralism is the organizing principle of the Leninist vanguard party, and Zinoviev's theses demand a rigidly disciplined, centralized party.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: opposed to privatizing public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states restricted strikes yet in capitalist states communists support them; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: Marxists attribute poverty to social institutions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: Leninist nationalities policy treats diversity as compatible with a united socialist state.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices are filled by elected and appointed cadres through institutional channels, not lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties accepted emergency measures against internal enemies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Ruling parties applying the principle put press under party direction; Lenin's 1906 position allows free debate within programme limits but not public breaking of party action.

party-commands-army.rationale: The CPC constitution says the army and militia must accept the centralised leadership of the Party.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: Paris Commune-derived Leninist principle of officials on workers' wages.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lenin's rule is full freedom of criticism but unity of action once the party decides, and the CPC constitution makes minority subordinate to majority.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred: opposed to the EU as a capitalist project, though the Comintern was a supranational centralist body.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The party and collective bodies, not a head of state, command; collective leadership is a principle.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: rule by religious scholars contradicts atheist materialism and party leadership of the state.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: Lenin's revolutionary defeatism in the First World War.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred: Communist states did censor art on ideological grounds, though not about virtue; split.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials by electors is part of the principle's application to the state, as in the 1977 Soviet constitution.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: Communist states joined alliances like the Warsaw Pact.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: Communist states used public rental housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: Marxists favored arming workers in revolution, while ruling parties built regular armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: Marxists criticized 'rural idiocy' and favored industrial development.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: Communist parties on both sides of Korea and Vietnam pursued reunification, others not.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Leninism values intellectuals as party cadres.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: officially all peoples are equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states used the death penalty, notably China.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: socialist education includes gender equality.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: Leninist nationalities policy supported minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: single law for all, secular.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: Leninists emphasize discipline and conformity to collective decisions.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: Chinese amendment of 2018 versus Deng's term limits show adherents split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: Bolsheviks dissolved the 1918 Constituent Assembly in favor of soviets.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: Communist states have justified discipline for development.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties favor collective leadership chosen via the hierarchy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states ran money through the state bank under party direction (Gosbank), so an independent price-stability bank cuts against the principle of party leadership of all state organs.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine says nothing on borders, and Lenin himself ceded territory for peace at Brest-Litovsk, so adherents lean against a rule that land is never traded.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist parties treat property as subordinate to society and collective ownership as the goal, though they go further than a trust model.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties that use democratic centralism describe the USSR as a socialist state, and the state-capitalist reading comes from their left critics.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties favour state planning and regulation, so precautionary state action fits, but the doctrine does not address it.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist states built alliances such as the Warsaw Pact, though the doctrine itself is organizational.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents split: ruling parties annexed territory by force at times, yet claim anti-imperialist principles; the doctrine is silent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties placed religious bodies under state control and confiscated church property as a matter of course.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: in ruling Communist states the head of state is a party leader, since the party leads all state organs.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties kept states unitary and centralized, and the CPC constitution makes the party lead state organs and army.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred: centralism subordinates lower bodies to higher ones, which cuts against distinct regional systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist materialism and state atheism reject divine rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties favour progressive taxation as a lever on class inequality.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions shape consciousness, so changing circumstances remakes people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Adherents split: formal socialist legality exists, yet the party stands above state organs in the CPC constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-era Communist states made space exploration a showpiece of socialist progress.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: Leninist soviet power rejects balancing elites against the people and separation of powers.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: the principle formally calls for collective leadership, though ruling parties often developed leader cults, so adherents lean against.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred adherents have no common line.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties differ, with Maoist-influenced ones stressing continuing class struggle; Soviet practice stressed party unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties carried out land reform in the USSR and China.

refugee-return.rationale: No documented position; the doctrine is organisational.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties prioritise class over nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties are secular and treat religion as a private matter or an obstacle.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties promoted secular dress and women's mobilisation.

common-currency.rationale: No documented position; ruling parties used national currencies, and the doctrine is organisational.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern stressed class internationalism over kinship of peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties opposed national-cultural autonomy as a separate national organisation.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: Comintern parties were told to organise where they live, in one centralised party per country.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is built on historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties directed the economy by state planning, not by competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: No documented position; the doctrine is organisational.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Party leads state organs, so courts and bodies are subordinate to party and state decisions; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties such as the CPC and CPSU set quotas for women's representation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: socialism in one country and the Soviet bloc economies used a largely closed trading system.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties promoted socialist emulation and moral appeals alongside material pay.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Comintern conditions required illegal work and preparation for revolution under a disciplined vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties abolished noble titles and class privileges.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The principle is organisational and silent on curricula; ruling parties differ, with Soviet and Chinese practice emphasising national history and class history in different periods.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Comintern conditions require support for colonial liberation movements and condemn imperialist rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from ruling parties that applied the principle, which promoted patriotic education; the principle itself is silent.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from Soviet nationality policy of promoting minorities, which was a form of preference; the principle itself is silent.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties put banking and credit under state control.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Leninism holds capitalism in its imperialist stage heads to general crisis, a premise of the Comintern conditions.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Leninist states pursued influence over former imperial lands while also condemning imperialism; adherents split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Soviet practice was autarkic while the CPC later chose integration; the principle itself is silent.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin and the Comintern held that imperialist super-profits corrupted a layer of workers; inferred as the Leninist position.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties subordinated private property and mandated equal treatment by law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The CPC constitution places party leadership over state organs, so an entrenched bill of rights limiting the state is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: Leninist anti-imperialism treats imperial partition of peoples as illegitimate.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: democratic centralism makes every organ elective from below, and Leninist parties reject hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: The minority must yield to the majority and execute decisions uniformly, so no member can veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Leninists hold that revolution against a state that breaks its own legality is legitimate, though they reject bourgeois constitutional framing.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: Lenin and the Comintern treat bourgeois parliaments as instruments to use, with soviets and the party leading.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist states adopted animal protection in law, but it is not a defining concern.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states used animals for food and research under welfare rules; no principled objection.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: Leninists seek to abolish class distinctions rather than rely on elite benevolence.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Members must take active part in party work and obey its discipline; withdrawal is condemned.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist theory holds that the media and culture of capitalism reproduce the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: Marxists accept cultural hegemony, though Leninists stress the coercive state.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Lenin's theory of imperialism says capital exports and colonies drain the periphery.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: proletarian internationalism opposes birth-based reservation of office.

party-own-road.rationale: Under the Comintern conditions member parties were bound to the International's decisions, though later Chinese and Yugoslav parties asserted their own road.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: Soviet and Chinese practice split between self-reliance and accepting aid within the socialist camp.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: internationalist Marxism-Leninism rejects revanchist territorial claims, though Soviet practice varied.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: class, not descent, is the basis of political leadership in Leninism.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern and Communist states made anti-fascism a founding doctrine, as in the German Democratic Republic.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Communist parties reject the equation of fascism and communism as an anti-communist device.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Marx and Lenin viewed the American Civil War as a struggle over slavery.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Communist states removed monuments of the old order.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties frame disadvantage by class, not as a men's issue.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties frame domestic violence within women's emancipation and see it as asymmetric.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Chinese Communists and others claim socialism with national characteristics, though Marxism-Leninism is universalist.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party leads the army and the gun must obey the party; an independent guardian role is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: Soviet policy aimed to socialise housework, and Kollontai-style feminism called for recognising care as labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from ruling Communist states, which promoted family duty and care of elders in law and practice.

office-by-exam.rationale: Ruling Leninist parties used both exams and party appointment, so adherents are split; no doctrine on this.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from Leninist ruling parties, which kept strategic industry under state control.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from Soviet and Chinese law, which liberalised divorce early; the principle itself does not address it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The CPC constitution has electors able to recall deputies, but the organisational principle subordinates them to higher bodies.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from Leninist ruling parties, which ran state pay-as-you-go pension systems and rejected private accumulation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from Soviet and Chinese practice of state or collective ownership of land, with users holding rights of use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: In ruling Communist states legislatures formally approved budgets but the party directed them, so adherents are split on real control.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from Soviet and Chinese practice, which promoted a common language while recognising others; not a doctrine of the principle.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Leninist ruling states, which held land as state or collective property and barred foreign ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from Marxism-Leninism's class-first view, which treats racial inequality as a product of capitalism rather than a disparate-impact test.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist critique of capitalist commodity culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Comintern conditions required parties to support liberation and revolutionary movements against imperial governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet Union's record under the Brezhnev Doctrine, as ruling parties applied the principle.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that bourgeois states serve capital.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from ruling communist states' practice of controlling foreign funding of civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by an organizational doctrine; Marxist-Leninist states have both promoted and curbed births.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine favours central decisions over local autonomy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from ruling communist states' guarantee of a right to work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's theory of imperialism, which ties war to capitalism rather than regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: the party demands obedience from members, but communist doctrine treats law as class instrument.

non-intervention.rationale: Ruling communist states invoke non-interference, while the Comintern supported intervention for revolution.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Comintern and ruling-party practice of industrial unions under party leadership.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: ruling communist states kept legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from secrecy in the party and communist states.

informal-organisation.rationale: The principle is permanent, hierarchical party organization with binding discipline, as the Comintern conditions and CPC constitution require.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the CPC constitution's stress on national sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist materialism and atheism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from Leninist anti-imperialism; Communist states have however demanded deference within their own blocs.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist parties centralise revenue and redistribute across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist distinction between personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Comintern conditions commit parties to revolution against capitalism and its supporters.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states favour state-run services over private provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist treatment of religion as an ideological relic.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that capitalism created the base for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Communist parties have framed women's emancipation as tied to socialist transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states promoted communal childcare and canteens.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from Leninist internationalism, though Communist states have run language-standardising campaigns.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Leninists backed national self-determination in principle but ruling parties have overridden agreements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties favour centralised state planning over small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's formal opposition to national oppression, though ruling parties encouraged settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Comintern conditions require breaking with reformism and socialist-capitalist third ways.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist parties that use the principle, whose internationalism subordinates national and religious land claims to class and the Comintern line.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the communist parties' anti-fascist stance.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist parties, which varied, though most opposed a legal criminalisation in theory.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the principle demands binding discipline and unity of action, and ruling parties applying it suppressed organised opposition, though it is an organisational rule, not a statement on the state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the materialist, atheist stance of the Marxist-Leninist parties that use it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Comintern conditions required parties to support colonial liberation movements and expose imperialist rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from the parties' materialism and the Comintern's line, which did not endorse religious war.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the parties' secular materialism, which rejects religious law as a basis for rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Debate is open before a decision, but decisions are made by elected organs and binding on all, so it is neither direct nor purely representative; the sources do not settle it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the parties that used it treated class as primary though they opposed racial oppression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and varied among the parties that use it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and varied among the parties that use it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from the parties' Marxist-Leninist class analysis, which treats left and right as distinct class camps.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist analysis that labour under capital is exploited and estranged, though the sources do not use the term.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the parties' internationalism, which treats culture-clash framings as divisive.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred from the parties' atheist materialism.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from ruling Communist states that kept religion out of state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no ideological position follows from the organisational principle.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist aim of replacing capitalism with planned socialism, though it allowed market periods.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from the parties' view that the proletarian state needs an army to defend the revolution.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; ruling parties such as the CPC later adopted it but the principle itself is silent.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Communist states have taken varied positions on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties reject hereditary rule in principle, though some ruling parties have in practice allowed it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties placed credit in state banks, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties are anti-imperialist and opposed outside financial control, though this is not part of the organizing doctrine itself.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties reject bourgeois democracy and the Soviet system tied political rights to class, not to property qualifications for voters.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the organizational doctrine; ruling Leninist parties have varied.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist theory of commodity fetishism that the parties using the principle inherit.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist view that bourgeois freedoms are formal, though ruling parties also controlled the press themselves.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern conditions demand illegal work and party discipline, and Leninist states governed by party directive as well as by statute.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties profess internationalism and equal rights regardless of race or ethnicity.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the principle predates the internet, and the CPC and other parties have used it both for control and for consultation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist parties kept internal records closed and the principle subordinates lower bodies to higher ones, not to the public.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties were officially atheist but did not generally legislate against interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from Leninist internationalism and opposition to religious or ethnic discrimination.

citizens-assembly.rationale: A disciplined party hierarchy decides, not lot-selected citizens; inferred from the pyramid structure of binding higher organs.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The principle is an organizational doctrine silent on religion, and Marxist-Leninist parties are hostile to religion rather than reforming it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist parties that apply the principle and their hostility to concentrated capital.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from ruling Leninist parties, which historically penalized homosexuality; the principle itself is silent.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from Comintern conditions requiring party propaganda against religion and from ruling parties' practice; low confidence.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from ruling Leninist parties, which relied on police and prisons and held the state would not be abolished before communism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Majority decision binding on the minority is the core of the principle, which leaves no room for communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist insistence that the party-state provides welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the 1973 CPC constitution sets no term limits, and ruling parties kept leaders in office for long periods.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the binding hierarchy of the party, which subordinates lower bodies to higher ones rather than letting voters withdraw mandates.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed by the principle; ruling parties were atheist and hostile to religious institutions.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from ruling Leninist parties' family laws proclaiming spousal equality; low confidence.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The principle concerns party organisation; ruling communist states have not usually given foreigners votes, but the doctrine itself is silent.

rent-control.rationale: The doctrine is organisational and silent on housing; ruling parties used both state allocation and controlled rents, so it is inferred as neutral.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist states, which kept state patent systems and some forms of copyright while rejecting private ownership of means of production.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist ruling parties, which organised drilled youth leagues such as the Komsomol and Young Pioneers, as the CPC constitution points to the Communist Youth League.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The doctrine is silent; Leninist states split, with the USSR and China holding nuclear weapons but others, such as Cuba, not hosting them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist anti-imperialism, which opposes foreign bases of rival blocs, though the USSR stationed its own forces abroad.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; ruling parties recognised some genocides selectively for political reasons, so no clear position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that socialism distributes by work, 'to each according to his work', and opposes income from owning capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Leninist parties hold revolutionary and defensive violence legitimate, and the Comintern conditions require armed struggle.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Marxist-Leninists treat nations as historical categories, though ruling parties promoted national tradition; inferred and mixed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; ruling parties have been socially conservative on the question but the doctrine is organisational.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Leninist parties historically prioritised class over gender categories but the question is outside the principle.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist states, which honoured fallen revolutionaries as 'martyrs' in public commemoration, though the term is not religious in this tradition.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is materialist and atheist and reads politics as class struggle, not a spiritual battle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from internationalism; Leninist states, however, practiced homeland-centred policy, so only mildly rejected.

culture-before-state.rationale: Leninists make seizing and holding state power the first task and treat culture as following the revolution, as the party's central aim is the state.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; atheist doctrine treats religion as ideology and takes no side on how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; Marxism-Leninism treats religion as ideology to be overcome, so no position on judging texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Comintern conditions demand equal treatment of nationalities and opposition to national chauvinism; majority control of the economy would contradict this.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-style states drew ethnic territorial units, but the doctrine is organisational and would not endorse merging regions around one people.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties treated unions as subordinate to the party, so independence from the ruling party is rejected.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Leninist programme rests on proletarian rule exercised through the party, the premise of the Comintern conditions.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist states placed basic services under public ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-type states used both bicameral and unicameral bodies; the doctrine itself does not address it.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: Leninist states vested productive property in the national state, not local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Lower bodies are bound to higher ones and the minority to the majority, so delegates merely coordinating while locals decide runs against the principle.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is organizational and does not address wage levels or family structure.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: no doctrinal stance on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: no doctrinal stance; Soviet-type states valued science but the principle does not address it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: a centralizing party-state seeks full visibility over finance and opposes untraceable money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: party-states expect identifiable participation and monitor communication.

person-over-state.rationale: The individual is subordinated to the organization under the principle, so treating persons as ends against the collective is rejected.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist materialism treats spiritual claims as secondary or illusory.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: higher organs hold authority over lower ones, which fits revocable regional powers in a unitary state.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist states promoted modern agricultural science.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-style planning favoured urban concentration and industrialization.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the Comintern and Leninist internationalism frame politics by class, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: internationalist class doctrine treats racial pride as a distraction from class solidarity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: Leninists opposed imperialist wars but endorsed revolutionary and civil wars, so adherents are split on this wording.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats nations as historical formations with a common language, but communist parties place class over nation and the principle itself is organisational.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Leninist parties favour unified class organisation across communities, and the principle is hostile to separate sectional bodies.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Ruling parties have at times voiced such claims, but the principle does not address the issue and parties using it differ.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist parties that use the principle, which commonly provide state-funded education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties prefer state planning and direct regulation to market-based charges.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from communist party programmes that stress long-term planning; the principle itself says nothing on the point.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist stress on equality and class unity rather than distinct gendered values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Parties using the principle have both backed disarmament diplomacy and built large armies; the organisational doctrine is silent.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Comintern conditions favoured disciplined, partly illegal party work, and ruling parties conducted diplomacy in secret; inferred from that practice.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: ruling Communist parties that apply the principle have kept state control over foreign exchange and capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Leninist parties' control of the army and state under party direction; no source discusses private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the principle of binding decisions and discipline; ruling parties demanded obedience in the armed forces.

collective-bargaining.rationale: In Leninist practice unions act under party leadership, and the Comintern conditions require party control of them.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: An organizational doctrine that takes no stand on tax credits; inferred only from Marxist-Leninist parties.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from planning by central party decision, which would not accept legal limits binding it.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Comintern conditions require support for liberation movements in the colonies, implying an anti-imperialist world order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred from Leninist doctrine that the bourgeois state must be broken and replaced by a proletarian one.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from planned economies run by one central party line, not open local experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The doctrine is organizational and bears no relation to ecological accounting.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Comintern line is internationalist, though ruling parties often used nationalism; inferred and low.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Organizational doctrine with no stated position on student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: No stated position; Leninist parties favoured national unity within states but supported colonial liberation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist views of human nature as shaped by social conditions.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from ruling Communist parties' direction of the press and broadcasting, which opposes independence from the state.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist materialism; ruling parties promoted atheism, though the doctrine itself is organizational.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from ruling Leninist parties, which planned agriculture under state direction; the doctrine itself is organizational.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from ruling Communist states such as the USSR and China, which built nuclear forces; the doctrine is organizational.

workers-own-party.rationale: Lenin's conception of the party as the working class's own independent vanguard is the point of democratic centralism, and the Comintern conditions require breaking with other parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from Soviet and Chinese ruling parties' law-making on women's emancipation; not discussed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from ruling parties that legislated women's equal rights, including inheritance; not stated in the doctrine.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming is not addressed by the doctrine; ruling parties handled language policy differently.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from state-directed economies, where the party and state regulate harm rather than private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The party leads all state organs under strict subordination, leaving no room for an advisory role for chiefs; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Ruling parties pursued state-led growth, but later put environmental limits in policy; inferred split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from party leadership over state organs including the courts, under which central rules bind judges.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Ruling parties had varied language policies; the doctrine is organizational and silent on this.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: in Leninist states unions served as party-led transmission belts with near-universal membership, so voluntary membership is not the model.

voter-id.rationale: An organizational doctrine that is silent on ballot rules; ruling parties managed elections in other ways.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties kept religion under state control and favoured state-sanctioned bodies, not equal standing.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Leninist parties hold that real democracy is class rule led by the party, so competitive elections alone do not make a government democratic; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; ruling parties varied over time between permissive and puritanical.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: ruling parties following this principle, such as the Chinese party, have used shutdowns for order and treat the party's authority as paramount.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the Leninist ruling parties built state-run welfare and planning, not a single cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: Leninist ruling parties granted women equal political rights and party posts, though power stayed with the party centre.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that religion upholds old hierarchies and women's subordination.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that racial divisions are products of class society and colonialism.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: ruling Leninist parties set up mass women's organizations such as the Zhenotdel and the All-China Women's Federation.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist parties' commitment to public ownership of the means of production.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist states' stress on state sovereignty and distrust of Western-led legal bodies.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the atheist materialism of the Leninist parties that use the principle.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Communist parties' formal commitment to women's equality; the principle itself does not address self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Comintern's admission conditions required defending existing Soviet republics, and the Leninist tradition defends the state economy.

indirect-election.rationale: In the principle, organs are elected from below and higher bodies are chosen by delegates of lower ones, as in the CPC constitution.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Leninist parties' hostility to religion and to privileged church status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from ruling Communist states' practice of autonomous regions for minorities, though the principle itself stresses centralism.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the principle's emphasis on decisions by the party and state, not local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address colonial borders, and Leninist states have taken both positions.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist aim of industrial development and abundance.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address it, and Leninist states have both protected and settled minority regions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Communist parties' formal stress on equality of the sexes in state duties.

missingStatements.text: Once a party has adopted a decision, no member may publicly campaign against it, though criticism beforehand should be free.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin's 1906 rule of universal freedom of criticism provided it does not disturb unity of a definite action.

missingStatements.text: Political parties should be organized as a hierarchy in which lower bodies are bound by the decisions of higher bodies.
missingStatements.rationale: The CPC constitution and the principle's pyramid structure subordinate lower levels to higher ones.

notes: Critics, including Deng Xiaoping (1980), held that centralism overwhelmed democracy in practice. Yugoslavia in 1974 and non-Leninist users of the term would answer many items differently.
